chunks.arabic_text: رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عِيسَى بْنِ عُبَيْدٍ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ رَاشِدٍ قَالَ:

translations.en: Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā ibn ʿUbayd narrated from al-Ḥasan ibn Rāshid, who said:

chunks.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ الْعَسْكَرِيَّ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ أَوْصَى بِمَالٍ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ

translations.en: I asked Abā al-Ḥasan al-ʿAskarī عليه السلام about a man who made a bequest of wealth in the way of Allah.
So he said: "The way of Allah is our Shi'ah."

en.summary: This hadith addresses the legal meaning of a bequest made "in the way of Allah." Imam Abū al-Ḥasan al-ʿAskarī عليه السلام explains that in this case it refers to support for their Shi'ah. The report thus connects a financial bequest with loyalty and service to the community of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام.
en.seo_question: What does "fī sabīl Allāh" mean in a bequest according to Imam al-ʿAskarī عليه السلام?

key_terms.فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ: in the way of Allah; here, a designated charitable or religious cause
key_terms.شِيعَتُنَا: our Shi'ah, meaning the followers of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام
